discovery: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated lattice models with ultracold atoms in optical lattices, including the bosonic and fermionic Mott insulators and single-site-resolved quantum gas microscopy

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München, Germany

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum many-body physics
motivation: Bloch, Esslinger and Greiner turned ultracold atoms in optical lattices into precise, tunable quantum simulators of condensed-matter models. The 2002 observation of the superfluid–Mott insulator transition (Greiner, Bloch) showed that the Hubbard model could be realised and controlled directly. Esslinger's experiments then brought fermions into lattices: Fermi surfaces, molecule formation, and in 2008 the fermionic Mott insulator, which Bloch's group observed independently. Greiner's and Bloch's quantum gas microscopes resolve individual atoms on individual lattice sites. They made it possible to see antiferromagnetic correlations, spin-charge dynamics and entanglement in the Fermi–Hubbard model directly. Together these advances created a new experimental field, analogue quantum simulation, now used worldwide to study high-temperature superconductivity, magnetism, many-body localisation and non-equilibrium dynamics. Their techniques are now standard tools and have led to programmable quantum matter.
